steps.text: Stir the oats, milk and salt together in a small pot.
Heat on medium, stirring often, until the porridge thickens and starts to bubble gently.
Mash half the banana with a fork until it looks creamy and smells sweet.
Stir the mashed banana and cinnamon into the porridge and cook one more minute.
Spoon into bowls and top with sliced banana, walnuts and a drizzle of honey.
Warm the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat until it loosens.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts and the pan hisses less.
Beat the eggs with pepper in a bowl until no streaks of white remain.
Pour the eggs into the pan and stir slowly until just set and creamy.
Crumble in the feta, fold once and serve at once with parsley on top.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the onion and pepper until the onion is soft and smells sweet.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook until the spices smell toasty.
Pour in the tomatoes and simmer until the sauce thickens and mounds on a spoon.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook until the whites are set but the yolks still wobble.
Scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan with bread.
Toast the bread until it is golden and crisp and smells nutty.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and salt until mostly smooth.
Crush the chickpeas lightly with a fork so some stay whole.
Spread the avocado over the toast and spoon the chickpeas on top.
Finish with chilli flakes if you like some heat, then eat while the toast is warm.
Warm the black beans and cumin in a small pan over medium heat.
Mash a third of the beans with a fork until the mixture turns thick and creamy.
Heat each tortilla in a dry pan until it is soft and speckled.
Slice the avocado and dice the tomato while the beans finish warming.
Fill the tortillas with beans, avocado and tomato, then squeeze lime over each.
Sprinkle with coriander and eat while the beans are still hot.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the diced pepper until it softens and the edges start to brown.
Crumble the tofu into the pan with the turmeric and salt.
Stir often until the tofu looks dry and smells warm and earthy.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts and the pan sounds quieter.
Serve the scramble hot, topped with the sliced spring onions.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes into bite-sized chunks and put them in a bowl.
Add the chickpeas and feta to the bowl.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and oregano in a cup until cloudy.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently until everything glistens.
Let the salad sit for five minutes so the juices mingle, then serve.
Drain the tuna and chickpeas well and tip them into a large bowl.
Flake the tuna with a fork until the pieces are bite-sized.
Add the tomatoes and spring onions to the bowl.
Stir the olive oil and lemon juice together, then pour over the salad.
Toss gently until the dressing coats everything and smells bright and sharp.
Top with parsley and serve with bread or leaves.
Grate the carrot and slice the cucumber into thin sticks.
Warm each tortilla in a dry pan for twenty seconds until pliable.
Spread three tablespoons of hummus down the middle of each tortilla.
Pile on the lettuce, carrot and cucumber, with a squeeze of lemon if you like.
Fold in the sides, roll tightly and slice in half.
Bring the water and ginger to a gentle simmer in a medium pot.
Add the noodles and cook until they are tender but still slightly chewy.
Slide in the tofu and spinach and warm until the spinach wilts.
Turn off the heat and let the broth stop bubbling.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of broth in a cup until smooth.
Stir the miso back into the pot and serve topped with spring onions.
Mash the beans roughly with the paprika and diced pepper in a bowl.
Spread the bean mixture over two tortillas and sprinkle with the cheddar.
Top each with a second tortilla and press down firmly.
Cook one quesadilla in a dry pan until the underside is golden and crisp.
Flip carefully and cook until the cheese melts and you hear a gentle sizzle.
Repeat with the second one, then cut into wedges and squeeze lime over.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the onion and carrots until the onion is soft and smells sweet.
Stir in the cumin and cook until the spices smell warm and toasty.
Add the lentils and stock and bring to a boil.
Simmer gently until the lentils collapse and the soup thickens.
Blend roughly with a stick blender, then stir in the lemon juice.
Taste, adjust the lemon, and cool before storing; the soup keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Soak the noodles in just-boiled water until tender but still springy.
Drain the noodles, rinse under cold water and shake them dry.
Simmer the prawns in a pot of water until they curl and turn pink.
Stir the lime juice, fish sauce and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the noodles, prawns, carrot, cucumber and mint with the dressing.
Taste and add more lime if it needs a sharper edge, then serve.
Rinse the rice, then simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered.
Spread the cooked rice on a tray and let it steam off until cool.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok until it shimmers and just begins to smoke.
Scramble the beaten eggs in the wok until they are just set.
Add the rice and peas and stir-fry until the grains separate and sizzle.
Splash in the soy sauce and sesame oil and toss through the spring onions.
Heat the oven to 200 C and line a tray with baking paper.
Pat the chickpeas very dry with a kitchen towel so they crisp.
Toss the chickpeas with the oil, paprika, cumin and salt on the tray.
Roast, shaking the tray halfway, until the chickpeas rattle and smell toasty.
Cool for five minutes so they crisp further, then eat within a day.
Mash the banana in a bowl until it looks like a smooth paste.
Stir in the peanut butter, honey and cinnamon until evenly mixed.
Fold in the oats until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Roll into twelve small balls using damp hands.
Chill the bites until they feel firm to the touch.
Blend the tahini and lemon juice in a food processor until pale and thick.
Add the garlic, chickpeas and half the water, then blend until smooth.
Add water a spoonful at a time until the hummus loosens and falls from a spoon.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with the olive oil.
Serve with the carrot and cucumber sticks for dipping.

recipes.title: Quick lemon hummus with crunchy sticks

steps.text: Toast the oats and cinnamon in a dry pan, stirring, until fragrant and lightly golden.
Tip the oats onto a plate and let them cool until crisp.
Spoon the yoghurt into two bowls while the oats cool.
Top with the blueberries, toasted oats and mixed seeds.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat until it loosens and shimmers.
Cook the onion until it is soft and smells sweet.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and curry powder and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the tomatoes and simmer until the sauce darkens and thickens.
Add the chickpeas and salt, then simmer until they are tender and the sauce clings.
Scatter with coriander; the curry keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the onion until it is soft and smells sweet.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin and cook until fragrant.
Add the lentils and water and bring to a boil.
Simmer, stirring now and then, until the lentils break down into a thick soup.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then add the lemon juice.
Taste for salt; the dal keeps for 3 days and thickens as it cools.
Heat the oven to 220 C and oil a large tray.
Mix the yoghurt, curry powder, garlic and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Turn the chicken through the marinade until every piece is coated.
Spread the chicken, peppers and onion on the tray in one layer.
Drizzle with the oil and roast until the chicken is browned at the edges.
Check the thickest piece is white throughout and the juices run clear, then rest.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the onion until soft and sweet-smelling, then add the garlic.
Stir in the sweet potato, cumin and paprika and cook until the spices smell toasty.
Add the tomatoes and half a can of water, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook until a fork slides easily into the sweet potato.
Stir in the beans and simmer until the chilli is thick.
Add the lime juice; the chilli keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Toss the chicken with the paprika, cumin and one tablespoon of oil.
Heat a large pan over high heat until a drop of water spits.
Sear the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and white throughout.
Move the chicken to a plate and add the remaining oil to the pan.
Fry the peppers and onion until the edges char and the onion smells sweet.
Warm the tortillas, then fill with chicken and vegetables and squeeze lime over.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Warm the oil and garlic in a pan until the garlic smells sweet, not brown.
Pour in the tomatoes and simmer until the sauce thickens and clings to a spoon.
Cook the spaghetti until it is tender with a slight bite in the centre.
Toss the drained pasta in the sauce with a splash of cooking water.
Tear in the basil and top with parmesan.
Cook the pasta in boiling salted water until tender with a slight bite.
Fry the mushrooms in the oil, undisturbed, until golden and the pan stops hissing.
Stir in the garlic and cook until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the cream and simmer until it thickens slightly.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts into the sauce.
Toss in the drained pasta, parmesan and pepper, loosening with cooking water.
Heat the oven to 200 C and find a baking dish.
Toss the tomatoes, garlic, oil and salt in a baking dish.
Roast the tomatoes until they burst and smell sweet.
Nestle the cod into the tomatoes and lay a lemon slice on each fillet.
Bake until the fish flakes easily and turns opaque all the way through.
Tear basil over the dish and spoon the juices onto the fish.
Rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in twice its volume of water.
Stir the soy sauce, honey and ginger together to make the glaze.
Sear the salmon skin side down in a pan until the skin sounds crisp.
Flip the salmon, pour in the glaze and simmer until it turns sticky.
Steam the broccoli over the rice pot until bright green and just tender.
Serve the salmon and broccoli over the rice with sesame seeds on top.
Simmer the rice covered in twice its volume of water until it is tender.
Pat the tofu dry and fry in the oil until golden and crisp on every side.
Add the broccoli and two tablespoons of water, then cover.
Steam until the broccoli is bright green and a knife slides in.
Stir the soy sauce, ginger, sugar and sesame oil together, then pour into the pan.
Toss for one minute until the sauce clings, then serve over the rice.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and stir in the curry powder and ginger.
Cook until the spices smell toasty and bloom in the oil.
Pour in the coconut milk and soy sauce and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the tofu, pepper and green beans and simmer until the beans are tender-crisp.
Stir in the lime juice, taste, and add more soy sauce if it needs salt.
Serve over steamed rice with extra lime wedges on the side.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until it shimmers and smokes lightly.
Fry the garlic and chillies until the aroma hits and they just colour.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until it is white throughout with browned edges.
Add the green beans and stir-fry until they turn bright and squeak between teeth.
Stir in the soy sauce and sugar until the sauce bubbles and coats everything.
Fold in the basil until it wilts and serve with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Thai basil chicken with green beans

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the spices, garlic and oil in a bowl.
Heat a large pan over high heat until a drop of water spits.
Fry the chicken in two batches until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Warm the pitas in a dry pan until soft and slightly puffed.
Split the pitas and spread each with yoghurt.
Fill with chicken and cucumber and eat while the chicken is hot.
Heat the oven to 220 C and line a large tray.
Toss the aubergine and chickpeas with the oil and cumin on a large tray.
Roast, turning once, until the aubergine is deeply golden and creamy inside.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and water until smooth and pourable.
Add water a spoonful at a time if the sauce feels stiff.
Spoon the roast vegetables onto plates, drizzle with sauce and scatter parsley.
Heat the oven to 220 C and find a large roasting tin.
Mix the oil, lemon juice, oregano, garlic and salt in a large roasting tin.
Add the potatoes and chicken and turn until coated.
Roast, turning once, until the potatoes are golden and the chicken browns.
Check the thickest thigh is white throughout and the juices run clear.
Rest for five minutes and spoon the tin juices over the top.
Simmer the rice covered in twice its volume of water until tender.
Heat the oil in a wok until it shimmers and fry the garlic and ginger.
Add the beef and break it up, cooking until browned and the sizzling quietens.
Add the green beans and stir-fry until bright and tender-crisp.
Stir in the soy sauce and sugar until the sauce bubbles and glazes the beef.
Spoon the beef and beans over the rice and serve hot.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until tender but springy, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok until it shimmers and add the garlic.
Stir-fry the prawns until they curl and turn pink and opaque.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry until it wilts and sounds less crisp.
Toss in the noodles, soy sauce and sesame oil until everything is hot.
Serve straight away while the noodles are glossy.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until a knife slides in without resistance.
Brown the beef in a wide pan until the sizzling quietens and the liquid is gone.
Add the onion and carrots and cook until the onion is soft and sweet-smelling.
Stir in the tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, peas and a splash of water, then simmer.
Mash the potatoes with the butter until smooth and spread over the beef.
Grill or bake the pie until the top is golden; it keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium-low heat.
Cook the leeks gently until they are soft and smell sweet, without browning.
Add the potatoes and stock and bring to a simmer.
Cook until the potatoes fall apart when pressed with a spoon.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the milk and pepper and reheat gently.
Taste for salt; the soup keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Boil the macaroni in salted water until tender with a slight bite.
Add the broccoli for the last two minutes, then drain both.
Melt the butter in a pot, stir in the flour and cook until it smells nutty.
Pour in the milk gradually, whisking, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cheddar and mustard until smooth.
Fold in the pasta and broccoli and serve while the sauce is silky.
Heat the oven to 220 C and line a large tray.
Toss the sweet potato with half the oil, paprika and salt on a tray.
Roast until the edges brown and a fork slides in easily.
Push the sweet potato aside and add the beans and salmon with the remaining oil.
Roast until the salmon flakes easily and the beans are blistered.
Serve with lemon wedges and squeeze them over everything at the table.
Simmer the rice covered in twice its volume of water until tender.
Cook the beef with the garlic, soy sauce and sugar until browned and glossy.
Wilt the spinach in a pan with the sesame oil, then squeeze out the water.
Fry the eggs in a lightly oiled pan until the whites are set and edges crisp.
Divide the rice among bowls and arrange the beef, spinach and grated carrot on top.
Crown each bowl with an egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Korean-style beef and spinach rice bowl

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the bread until golden and crisp.
Add the garlic, paprika and cumin and cook until fragrant, but do not let them burn.
Blend half the bread and spices with the water into a thick paste.
Return the paste to the pan with the chickpeas and simmer until thickened.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then add the vinegar.
Taste for salt; the stew keeps for 3 days and tastes better the next day.
Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat until deep golden and smelling sweet.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and tomato paste and cook until the paste darkens.
Add the paprika and chilli flakes and stir for thirty seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils and water and bring to a boil.
Simmer, stirring often, until the lentils melt into a thick stew.
Season with salt; the stew keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 1 tsp salt, plus a pinch for the yoghurt

steps.text: Stir the yoghurt, grated garlic and a pinch of salt together, then spread it across four shallow plates.
Bring a deep pot of water to a boil and stir in the vinegar and a generous pinch of salt.
Crack each egg into a sieve for a few seconds so the thin, watery white drains away.
Take the pot off the heat, slide the eggs in gently, cover, and leave until the whites set.
Melt the butter in a small pan until it sputters, then stir in the paprika and remove from the heat.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon, set one on each yoghurt bed and spoon the red butter over.
Season with a pinch of salt and serve straight away with warm pita for dipping.

ingredients.text: 400 g aubergine, sliced into thin rounds

steps.text: Rub the aubergine rounds with half the oil and a little salt, then grill until deep golden on both sides.
Stack the hot slices in foil, wrap tightly and leave them to steam until the skins loosen.
Peel off the skins, then blend the aubergine with tahini, garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Toss the chickpeas with the turmeric, cumin, paprika and a splash of water, mashing about half with a fork.
Fry the chickpeas in the remaining oil over medium heat, stirring now and then, until hot and golden.
Stir in four to six spoonfuls of the dip and cook until the scramble turns dry and golden.
Spoon into bowls with the leftover dip; the chickpea scramble keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 100 g kale, stems removed and chopped

steps.text: Warm a teaspoon of oil in a saucepan, then stir in the oats and one grated garlic clove.
Pour in the water, bring to a simmer, then cook on low, stirring often, until creamy.
Off the heat, stir in the miso and soy sauce until the oats taste savoury and rounded.
Cook the kale in a teaspoon of oil until tender and bright.
Stir the remaining garlic through the kale, then tip it into a bowl and keep it warm.
Fry the mushrooms in the same pan with the last teaspoon of oil until golden and tender.
Divide the oats between two bowls and top with the kale, mushrooms and sliced avocado.
Scatter over the sesame seeds and serve; the savoury oats keep for 3 days in the fridge.
Whisk the eggs with half the salt until evenly combined, then set the bowl aside.
Warm the oil in a wide, heavy pan and cook the onion with the remaining salt until soft and golden.
Stir in the ginger, garlic and chilli and cook until the raw smell fades and it turns fragrant.
Add the diced tomato and cook until it begins to soften and collapse into the onion.
Pour in the eggs and stir slowly and constantly until they form soft, moist curds.
Sprinkle over the curry powder and coriander, mix through, and serve hot with toast or flatbread.

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, for greasing the pan

steps.text: Beat the eggs until smooth, then stir in the carrot, spring onion, salt and sesame oil.
Warm a nonstick pan over medium-low heat and wipe it lightly with oil.
Pour in a thin layer of egg, swirl to coat, and cook until set below but wet on top.
Fold about an inch of egg over, then keep rolling toward you, leaving a short tail.
Slide the roll aside, oil the space, pour a thin layer under the tail, and roll again.
Repeat with the remaining egg until the roll is thick, then rest it on a board to cool a little.
Slice the roll into eight thick pieces and serve it warm.
Warm the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat until it shimmers.
Add the onion, tomatoes, chilli, garlic and salt and cook until softened and fragrant.
Pour in the beaten eggs with the torn tortilla pieces and stir gently to scramble.
Fold in the cheddar, take the pan off the heat, and let it melt into the eggs.
Scatter with coriander and serve straight away, tucked into warm tortillas if you like.

ingredients.text: 700 g sweetcorn kernels, fresh or frozen

steps.text: Cut the kernels from the cobs if using fresh corn; frozen kernels can go straight into the pan.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over high heat, then stir in the garlic for ten seconds.
Add the corn and salt, and cook for about five minutes, stirring now and then, until golden in patches.
Tip the hot corn into a large bowl and stir in the mayonnaise, yoghurt, lime juice and parmesan until creamy.
Fold through the coriander and spring onions, then taste for lime and salt and serve warm or at room temperature.

ingredients.text: 100 g kale, stems removed and chopped

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C and line a baking tray with parchment.
Simmer the quinoa in a cup of water for about 15 minutes, until all the water is absorbed.
Pat the chickpeas dry, toss with a tablespoon and a half of oil and salt, then spread out.
Roast the chickpeas for 15 to 20 minutes until crisp and golden, then cool so they crunch up further.
Whisk the lemon juice, remaining oil, mustard, sugar and a pinch of salt together in a large bowl.
Add the kale and massage it with your hands for a few minutes until it darkens and softens.
Toss in the quinoa and seeds, then stir through the cooled chickpeas just before serving.

recipes.title: Lemony quinoa kale salad with crispy chickpeas

ingredients.text: 225 g green beans, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
60 g red onion, very thinly sliced

steps.text: Boil the green beans in well salted water for 2 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Lift the beans into iced water to stop the cooking, then drain and pat them dry.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, grated garlic and salt together in a large bowl until cloudy.
Toss the chickpeas, kidney beans, parsley, celery, onion and green beans with the dressing until everything glistens.
Serve now or chill an hour first; the bean salad keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Shake the garlic, mustard, oil, vinegar, oregano and salt in a jar until the dressing turns cloudy.
Put the halved tomatoes, mozzarella and most of the basil into a large bowl.
Pour over the dressing and toss gently so the cheese stays whole.
Move everything to a shallow bowl, scatter over the remaining basil and serve straight away.
Put the couscous and salt in a bowl, cover with boiling water and a plate, and leave to swell.
Boil the whole broccoli head for about four minutes, until bright green and tender.
Lift out the broccoli and leave it to steam dry in a colander for a minute or two.
Grate the garlic into a jar and add the almonds, olive oil, orange juice and most of the chopped mint.
Seal the jar and shake until the dressing looks glossy.
Chop the broccoli finely, fluff the couscous with a fork, then mix the two together.
Spoon over half the dressing, crumble on the feta and scatter with the remaining mint.

ingredients.text: 3 ripe avocados, peeled, pitted and diced

steps.text: Chop the onion, chilli, coriander and a big pinch of salt together on a board.
Press and smear the pile with the flat of the knife until it turns into a rough green paste.
Scrape the paste into a bowl, add the diced avocado and mash with a spoon, leaving it chunky.
Fold in the diced tomato, then taste and add more salt until the flavours sing.
Grate or finely dice the cucumbers and squeeze out the extra water with your hands.
Crush the garlic and stir it into the yoghurt with the oil, lemon juice and salt.
Fold in the cucumber, then serve now or chill for an hour so the dip thickens.
Warm the pita until soft and cut into wedges; the tzatziki keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 1 small shallot or onion, very thinly sliced
2 spring onions, green parts finely sliced

steps.text: Bash the cucumbers with a rolling pin until the skins split, then halve and cut into chunks.
Toss the chunks with the salt and leave them for 30 minutes so the water drains out.
Pour away the liquid, then whisk the vinegar, soy sauce and sesame oil until slightly thick.
Toss the cucumber with the dressing, thinly sliced onion, spring onion, chilli flakes and sesame seeds until glossy.

ingredients.text: 2 cm piece of ginger, roughly chopped
150 g broccoli, cut into small florets
80 g brown rice, cooked, or a 200 g cooked pouch

steps.text: Fry the tempeh in hot oil in a wok until golden and charred, then lift out.
Stir-fry the sliced onion in the same pan until softened, then add garlic, ginger and chilli until fragrant.
Add the broccoli with a splash of water, cover briefly and steam until bright green and just tender.
Stir in the soy sauce and sugar, return the tempeh and toss until everything is sticky and glossy.
Serve the stir-fry over warm cooked brown rice.

ingredients.text: 2 tins red kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Warm the oil in a lidded pan and let the cumin seeds sizzle for about 20 seconds.
Add the garlic for a minute, then stir in the tomatoes, ginger, chilli and turmeric.
Turn the heat up and cook, breaking up the tomato, for about 10 minutes until thick and jammy.
Add the drained beans and water, cover, and simmer until the beans are soft and the sauce clings.
Stir through the coriander, loosen with a little water if needed; the rajma keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 300 g cauliflower, cut into bite-sized pieces
60 g green beans, trimmed and halved

steps.text: Cook the rice following the packet instructions so it is ready when the curry is.
Soften the onion, pepper and ginger in the oil over medium heat until the onion turns translucent.
Stir in the curry powder for a minute, then pour in the coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add the cauliflower, turn down the heat and simmer for 5 minutes, then add the green beans.
Simmer for 10 more minutes until the cauliflower is tender and the sauce is creamy.
Squeeze in the lime juice and serve over the rice; the curry keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 680 g portobello and shiitake mushrooms, sliced

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms into thick strips, then halve each strip so the pieces hold their shape.
Brown the portobellos in half the butter with salt, then the shiitakes in the rest, until golden but firm.
Return everything to the pan, sprinkle over the flour and toss for 30 seconds until it coats the mushrooms.
Stir in the stock, soy sauce and mustard, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer until slightly thickened.
Meanwhile cook the egg noodles in salted water following the packet, then drain.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the yoghurt and parsley until creamy.
Serve over the noodles; the stroganoff keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 1 small handful mint leaves, finely sliced

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan) and line a baking tray with foil.
Zest one lemon, then mix zest, half the juice, spices, garlic, half the spring onions and 2 tsp oil.
Spoon the mixture over the salmon in a shallow dish and leave for 10 minutes.
Mix the couscous with the leftover lemon juice, remaining oil, spring onions and 150 ml boiling water, then cover.
Roast the salmon on the foil with its marinade, drizzling with honey for the last 5 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork, fold in the mint, and serve with the salmon and lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Spiced honey salmon with lemon couscous

steps.text: Grate the ginger, squeeze its juice into a bowl, and set a teaspoon of the pulp aside.
Toss the pork in the ginger juice with half a tablespoon of soy sauce and 1 tablespoon of water.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce and water with the miso, sugar and reserved ginger in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Lay the pork in a single layer in the hot oil and leave it until golden underneath.
Flip the pork and cook until no pink remains.
Pour in the sauce and turn the pork until glossy and coated.
Pile the pork beside shredded cabbage on plates; the miso ginger pork keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 2 white fish fillets (180 g each), about 1.5 cm thick
4 spring onions, green parts, sliced on the diagonal
20 g fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks
1 red chilli, deseeded and cut into fine strips

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan) and lay each fillet on baking paper over foil.
Season both sides of the fish with salt and pepper, then fold the paper and foil into sealed parcels.
Bake the parcels until the fish flakes easily when pressed with a fork.
Fold the parcels open into boats and rest 3 minutes while the oil heats in a small pan.
Pile the spring onion, ginger and chilli on the fish and drizzle over the soy sauce and sesame oil.
Pour the hot oil over the topping so it sizzles loudly, then serve at once from the foil boats.

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Dijon mustard and 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard
1 to 2 tbsp water, to loosen the sauce

steps.text: Season the chicken thighs on both sides with two thirds of the salt and half of the pepper.
Sear the chicken in the oil over medium-high heat, smooth side down, until deep golden.
Turn the chicken and cook the other side until cooked through, then move to a plate.
Scrape out any loose black specks, keeping the browned film stuck to the pan.
Stir the cream, both mustards and remaining seasoning into the pan over medium heat, scraping up the browned bits.
Thin with water if needed and spoon over the chicken; the mustard chicken keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 285 g canned tuna in oil, drained
2 tbsp olive oil (or the oil from the tuna)
240 ml starchy pasta cooking water, reserved

steps.text: Boil the pasta in well salted water for a minute less than the packet says.
Scoop out a mug of the starchy cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Warm the oil in the empty pot with the garlic and chilli flakes for a minute.
Tip in the pasta with a splash of the cooking water and toss until it turns glossy.
Off the heat, fold in the tuna, parsley, lemon zest and juice, salt and pepper, keeping some chunks.
Soften the chopped pepper and spring onions in a pan with a splash of water for three minutes.
Add the beans, sliced mushrooms and halved tomatoes, then heat gently, stirring often, until piping hot.
Toast the bread while the beans heat, until it smells nutty and turns golden.
Spoon the saucy beans over the toast and serve straight away while hot.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of the salt, then cut the tomatoes into small wedges.
Heat two tablespoons of oil in a wok, pour in the eggs and scramble until just set, then lift out.
Stir-fry the tomatoes and spring onion in the remaining oil with the sugar and salt, covered, until soft.
Return the eggs, add a splash of water if dry, and toss until the sauce turns glossy.
Stir the oats and water together in a large microwave-safe bowl.
Microwave on high for one minute, stir, then microwave for another minute.
Keep heating in thirty second bursts, stirring each time, until the oats are thick and creamy.
Fold in the chopped apple, dust with cinnamon and drizzle with honey, then eat while warm.
Crumble the feta into a food processor and add the yoghurt, half the oil and the pepper.
Blend for a few minutes, scraping down the sides, until the dip is smooth and fluffy.
Swirl it into a shallow bowl and drizzle with the honey and remaining oil.
Toast the pita and tear it into strips. Covered in the fridge, the dip keeps for 3 days.
Melt one teaspoon of butter in a small frying pan over medium-low heat.
Cut a small hole in the middle of each slice and set one in the pan.
Crack an egg into a cup, tip it into the hole and cook until the white turns opaque.
Flip and cook another minute until the yolk is set, then repeat with the second slice and top with avocado.
Toast the bread slices until crisp and golden at the edges, a few minutes per side.
Grate the tomatoes on a box grater, discard the skins and stir the pulp with the salt.
Rub the cut side of the garlic over the warm toast, then drizzle with olive oil.
Spoon the tomato over each slice and serve at once, before the juice soaks through.
Whisk the eggs, milk and cinnamon together in a shallow dish until smooth.
Lay in the bread and soak for two minutes, then turn and soak the other side.
Melt the butter in a frying pan and fry the slices in batches, three minutes per side.
Pile onto plates and scatter the blueberries over the warm toast to serve.

ingredients.text: 150 g mature cheddar, sliced or grated

steps.text: Heat the grill to high and toast the bread on both sides until golden.
Spread each slice with mustard, then cover edge to edge with sliced or grated cheddar.
Shake over the Worcestershire sauce and grill for two to three minutes until golden and bubbling.
Season with black pepper and eat straight away while the cheese is molten.
Mix the baked beans, chopped onion and pepper, smoked paprika and grated cheddar together in a bowl.
Spread the filling over half of each tortilla and fold the other half over it.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan, add two quesadillas, cover and fry about a minute per side.
Repeat with the rest, cut each into wedges and serve while the cheese is melted.
Heat the oven to 190C and bake the bread slices on a tray until lightly browned.
Peel ribbons from the cucumber with a vegetable peeler while the toast bakes.
Spread a thick layer of hummus over each toast, then pile on the cucumber ribbons.
Crumble over the feta, drizzle with olive oil and finish with a sprinkle of chilli flakes.
Lower the eggs into boiling water and boil for eight minutes, then cool them in cold water.
Peel the eggs and mash roughly with the mayonnaise and mustard until creamy but still chunky.
Stir in the finely diced celery and sliced spring onion until evenly mixed.
Toast the bread on one side, fill with the egg mayo, and cut each sandwich in half.
Heat the grill to high. Mash the tuna with the celery and mayonnaise using a fork.
Toast the bread on both sides until golden, then spread each slice lightly with butter.
Pile the tuna mixture onto the toast, spreading it to the edges, and top with cheese.
Grill for one to two minutes until the cheese is golden and bubbling, then serve hot.
Bring the stock to a boil in a medium pot, then stir in the rice.
Simmer on low until the rice is tender and the grains look plump.
Beat the egg whites until frothy and thick, then whisk in the yolks and lemon juice.
Whisking all the time, drizzle in two ladles of hot stock so the eggs do not curdle.
Pour it back into the pot on low heat, stirring until slightly thick. Do not let it boil.

ingredients.text: 750 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Warm the oil in a soup pot and soften the onion for 5 minutes until sweet.
Stir in the garlic, then add the stock, tomatoes, beans, pepper, paprika and cumin.
Bring to the boil, then simmer partly covered for 10 minutes.
Let it cool a little, then blend most of the soup, leaving some chunky.
Stir in the lime juice and season to taste. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Heat the oven to 180C, brush the pita with oil and salt, then bake until crisp.
Whisk the remaining oil with the lemon juice, cumin, garlic, a pinch of salt and pepper.
Tear the lettuce into a big bowl and add the tomatoes, cucumber and mint.
Break the cooled pita into pieces, add them, and toss with most of the dressing.
Scatter the feta over the top and serve straight away so the pita stays crunchy.

ingredients.text: 2 thick slices slightly stale sourdough or ciabatta

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Tear the bread into chunks and toast until crisp and golden.
Press the two ripest tomatoes through a sieve over a large bowl and discard the skins.
Chop the remaining tomatoes and add them to the bowl with the cucumber and red onion.
Add the cooled bread, drizzle in the oil, tear in half the basil, and toss well.
Rest for 10 minutes, then season, toss again and top with the remaining torn basil.

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, plus extra to serve

steps.text: Heat the grill to its highest setting and line a baking tray with baking parchment.
Warm the milk in a small pan, then whisk in the mustard and chilli flakes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cheese and Worcestershire sauce until melted.
Beat in the egg yolk, then toast the bread and spread the cheese mixture thickly on top.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve with extra Worcestershire sauce.

ingredients.text: 190 g green or brown lentils, rinsed
1 medium carrot, peeled and left whole

steps.text: Put the lentils, garlic, onion, whole carrot and wine in a pan and cover with water by 2 cm.
Boil, then simmer gently for about 15 minutes, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
Meanwhile whisk the mustard, vinegar, oil and salt in a large bowl until creamy.
Drain the lentils, discard the garlic and onion, and dice the carrot into small pieces.
Toss the warm lentils, carrot and parsley through the dressing. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Bring a pot of water to the boil for the noodles, then mince the garlic and ginger.
Stir the garlic, ginger, peanut butter and hot water in a serving bowl until loose and smooth.
Whisk in the soy sauce, fish sauce, sesame oil and lime juice until the sauce looks glossy.
Cook the noodles as the packet says, then drain, keeping a splash of the cooking water.
Toss the hot noodles in the sauce, loosening with a spoonful of cooking water if needed.
Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Move the eggs to a bowl of iced water and leave until cool enough to peel.
Peel and mash the eggs, then mix in 2 tbsp mayonnaise, the yoghurt, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Spread the mustard and remaining mayonnaise over the bread, then spoon the egg salad onto two slices.
Top with the other slices, press gently, trim the crusts if you like, and cut in half.
Warm the oil in a medium pot and cook the garlic for a minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes with their juices, then the stock, sugar, salt and pepper, breaking up the tomatoes.
Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until the tomatoes turn soft and sweet.
Blend with a hand blender until smooth, then stir in the basil and cream.
Ladle into bowls and top with parmesan. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Bring the rice and water to the boil, cover, and cook on low for 12 minutes.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and fry the eggs sunny-side up until the whites set.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls and rest a thin slice of butter on each.
Slide an egg onto each bowl and drizzle with the soy sauce and sesame oil.
Sprinkle over the sesame seeds, then break the yolk and stir everything through the rice.

ingredients.text: 240 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Mash the chickpeas in a large bowl until about half are crushed, for a tuna-like texture.
Stir in the mustard, mayonnaise, celery, onion, lemon juice, parsley, salt and pepper.
Taste, and add more lemon or salt if it needs it. Toast the bread until golden.
Pile the salad onto two slices and close with the others. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 142 g canned tuna in water, drained

steps.text: Stir the yoghurt, lemon juice, oregano and pepper together in a bowl to make the sauce.
Drain the tuna and flake it into the sauce, mixing until well coated.
Fold in the cucumber, tomatoes and feta, then season with a little salt to taste.
Cut each pita in half, spoon the filling into the pockets, and sprinkle with parsley.
Stir the vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, pepper and sugar together in a bowl, then toss in the chicken.
Leave it to marinate for 15 minutes while you start the rice cooking.
Shake the marinade off the chicken and brown it in the hot oil for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the leftover marinade, bring it to a boil, then turn down and simmer for 10 minutes.
Turn the chicken and simmer another 10 minutes, until the sauce is reduced by half and glossy.
Serve over the rice, scattered with spring onion. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 120 g firm tofu, cut into strips
1 medium potato (about 200 g), cut into small dice

steps.text: Boil the diced potato in salted water for 6 minutes, until just tender.
Add the noodles to the same pot for 4 minutes, then drain well and shake dry.
Fry the tofu strips in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Fry the garlic and chilli in the remaining oil for 20 seconds, then stir in soy sauce, sugar and ketchup.
Add the noodles, potato and tofu, and toss over high heat until coated and fairly dry.
Push everything aside, scramble the egg in the gap, then fold the noodles back over it and serve.

ingredients.text: 300 g long-grain white rice, to serve

steps.text: Start the rice cooking. Stir the soy sauce, chilli flakes, garlic, sesame oil, sugar and water into a sauce.
Slice the tofu into 1 cm pieces and pat them gently dry with kitchen paper.
Fry the tofu in the hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until golden and crisp.
Lay the onion over the tofu, pour the sauce on and bring it to a boil.
Cover and braise on medium-low for 5 minutes, until the sauce clings and the onion is soft.
Spoon over the rice. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Rinse the lentils under cold water until the water runs clear.
Put them in a pot with 350 ml water, the onion, garlic, ginger, chilli, spices and salt, then boil.
Turn to medium, cover, and cook for 15 minutes until the lentils are soft and the water is absorbed.
Stir in the coconut milk and remaining 250 ml water, then simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Taste for salt and serve with rice or flatbread. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel, and prick each with a fork.
Meanwhile, cook the onions in 2 tbsp oil for about 8 minutes, until golden and no longer raw smelling.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for a minute, then the tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes until mushy.
Add the curry powder and salt, cook until fragrant, then pour in the water. Cover and simmer 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, fry the eggs in the last tbsp of oil for 3 minutes until golden and blistered.
Slip in the eggs, simmer 2 minutes, and finish with coriander. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 2 medium potatoes, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
1 small cauliflower (about 250 g), in small florets

steps.text: Soften the onion in the hot oil for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Stir in the turmeric and curry powder for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until they break down into a thick gravy.
Pour in the stock, add the potatoes, cover, and simmer for 6 minutes.
Stir in the cauliflower and cook, covered, for 10 minutes until the potato is tender and the cauliflower has bite.
Uncover and cook briefly until the sauce clings, then salt to taste. It keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Cook the onion in the hot oil for 6 minutes, until soft and lightly browned.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for a minute, then add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until thick.
Add the curry powder and cook for a few seconds, until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes, until creamy. Stir in the salt and lime juice.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until pink and cooked through. Serve with rice.

ingredients.text: 600 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, in bite-sized pieces
30 g fresh ginger, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and pepper, and rest 10 minutes.
Heat the oil and remaining sugar in a wide pan until it turns dark amber, about 3 minutes.
Add the ginger, garlic and onion for 30 seconds, then the chicken, tossing until lightly tinted.
Pour in the water, cover, and simmer gently for 10 minutes, tossing halfway.
Uncover and cook 8 to 10 minutes more, until the sauce turns syrupy and the chicken is cooked through.
Scatter with spring onion and serve with rice. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Cook the rice, then spread it on a tray to cool and dry while you prepare everything else.
Stir the soy sauce and sugar together to make a quick sweet soy, and slice the chicken thinly.
Fry the chilli and garlic in 1 tbsp oil for 10 seconds, add the onion, and cook for a minute.
Add the chicken and stir until no pink remains, then pour in half the sweet soy for a minute.
Add the cooled rice, remaining sweet soy and fish sauce, and stir constantly until the grains caramelise.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites set and crisp, then top each portion.
Cook the rice, then spread it on a tray to cool and dry while you prepare everything else.
Stir-fry the prawns in 1 tbsp hot oil for 2 minutes until pink, then set them aside.
Fry the garlic and onion in the same wok for a minute, then add the rice, breaking up clumps.
Push the rice aside, add 1 tbsp oil and the eggs, scramble gently, and mix them through.
Add the carrot, soy sauce and sugar, and stir-fry for 3 minutes until the carrot is just tender.
Return the prawns, toss in the tomato for a minute, and serve while hot.
Dice the onion and pepper finely so they melt into the sauce as it simmers.
Brown the beef with the onion and pepper in a wide pan until no pink remains.
Stir in the tomatoes, ketchup and Worcestershire sauce, then season with salt and pepper.
Simmer on medium-low, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Spoon onto toasted buns or serve on its own. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 700 g thick white fish fillets, cut into large chunks
2 bell peppers, one red and one green, sliced

steps.text: Toss the fish chunks with the lime juice and half the garlic, then set aside.
Soften the sliced onion in the olive oil for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the peppers and remaining garlic and cook for 3 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the tomatoes and paprika and cook for 3 minutes until they begin to break down.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 4 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Nestle in the fish, spoon sauce over it and cook 4 minutes, without stirring, until opaque and flaking.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, then cool them in cold water and peel.
Poach the fish in 400 ml water for 8 minutes, then flake it and keep the water.
Simmer the rice in the poaching water, covered, for 10 minutes, adding the peas for the last 3.
Meanwhile, soften the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, then stir in the curry powder for a minute.
Rest the rice off the heat for 3 minutes, then fold in the onion, fish, parsley, lemon juice and salt.
Top with the halved eggs. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Peel and dice the apples, then simmer with a splash of water and the cinnamon until soft.
Mash the apples roughly with a fork and keep the sauce warm while you fry.
Grate the potatoes and onion finely, then wring out as much liquid as you can in a towel.
Mix the potato and onion with the eggs, flour and salt into a tacky batter.
Fry flattened scoops of batter in hot oil, 3 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and crisp.
Drain briefly on kitchen paper and serve hot with the warm applesauce.

ingredients.text: 400 g potatoes, peeled and cut into small pieces

steps.text: Cut the potatoes into small bite-sized pieces and slice the onion thinly.
Cook both in the olive oil over medium heat, stirring, for 12 minutes until the potato is just tender.
Lift them out, leave 1 tablespoon oil in the pan, and season with salt, pepper and paprika.
Whisk the eggs until fluffy, then stir in the seasoned potato and onion.
Pour the egg mixture into the pan, cover, and cook on low until the base browns.
Flip the omelette onto a plate, slide it back and cook until set, then sprinkle with spring onion.

ingredients.text: 500 g chicken breast, sliced into thin cutlets

steps.text: Season the cutlets with salt and half the oregano, then brown them in the oil, 3 minutes per side.
Lift the chicken out, then cook the sliced courgette, pepper and diced carrot in the pan for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and tomatoes with the rest of the oregano, then boil for 1 minute.
Return the chicken and simmer for 18 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Spoon the sauce over the chicken. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Roast the tomato at 200C for 12 minutes until the skin blisters and softens.
Meanwhile, fry the rice in the oil, stirring often, until it turns opaque and golden brown.
Blend the roasted tomato with the onion and garlic, adding a spoonful of stock if needed.
Stir the puree into the rice for a few minutes, then add the stock and salt.
Bring to a light boil, then cover and simmer on medium-low until the liquid is absorbed.
Switch off the heat and leave the rice covered to steam for 5 minutes, then fluff.

ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp salt, plus extra for the aubergine

steps.text: Salt the aubergine cubes well and leave them in a sieve for 15 minutes.
Warm 1 tablespoon oil with the garlic, add the tomatoes, half the basil and the sugar, then simmer.
Squeeze the aubergine dry, then fry it in the remaining oil until golden brown.
Boil the pasta in salted water until al dente, then drain, keeping a splash of the water.
Toss the pasta with the sauce, loosening it with pasta water, and season with salt.
Top with the aubergine, crumbled feta and the remaining basil.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water until al dente and keep a mug of the cooking water.
Soften the chopped onion and garlic in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook for about a minute until just wilted.
Blend the spinach mixture with the basil, milk, feta and walnuts until completely smooth.
Warm the sauce in the pan, add the pasta and toss with a splash of cooking water.
Season with salt and pepper and serve straight away.
Boil the pasta in well salted water until al dente, then drain.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter with the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the prawns for 2 minutes, flip, add the garlic and cook 2 minutes more until pink.
Add the wine and remaining butter and simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Off the heat, stir in the lemon zest and juice, chilli flakes and parsley.
Toss with the pasta and serve straight away.

ingredients.text: 225 g thin spaghetti, broken into 2.5 cm pieces

steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic until completely smooth.
Toast the broken pasta in the oil over medium-low heat, stirring, until golden brown.
Lift the pasta into a bowl, then bring the puree, stock, salt and cumin to a boil.
Stir the toasted pasta back in and simmer for 7 to 8 minutes until just tender.
Ladle into warm bowls and scatter with chopped coriander while it is steaming hot.

ingredients.text: 600 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 1/2 tbsp curry powder, preferably a dark roasted one

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the curry powder and leave it to flavour while you prepare the rest.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and chillies and fry for two minutes until fragrant.
Add the spiced chicken and chopped tomato, stirring until the tomato starts to collapse.
Pour in the water, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and cook uncovered for eight minutes until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt to taste and serve with rice. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 450 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 medium sweet potato, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps.text: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and the sweet potato into 2 cm cubes.
Cook the onion in the oil for five minutes, then stir in the ginger and garlic.
Turn up the heat, add the chicken and stir for two minutes until pale outside.
Stir in the tomatoes, sweet potato and salt, and lower the heat to medium.
Whisk the peanut butter with the hot stock until smooth, then stir it into the pan.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the sweet potato is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Taste, adjust the salt and serve with rice. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Blend the tomatoes, peppers, onion and chilli until completely smooth.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the blended mixture for ten minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the tomato paste, curry powder, salt and stock, then simmer for five minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, stir once, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
Check once halfway and add a splash of water if the pot looks dry.
Rest off the heat, covered, for five minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Covered in the fridge, any leftover rice keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 2 boneless pork loin chops, about 100 g each
3 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying
150 g green cabbage, very finely shredded
2 tbsp sesame seeds, lightly toasted and crushed

steps.text: Shred the cabbage very finely and chill it while you prepare the pork.
Stir the ketchup and Worcestershire sauce into a dipping sauce, then mix in the crushed sesame seeds.
Slit the connective tissue, pound the chops gently, then season both sides with salt.
Coat each chop in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Heat 3 cm of oil to 170C, fry each chop one minute per side, then rest four minutes.
Raise the heat to 180C and fry again for 30 seconds per side until deep golden.
Slice the cutlets into strips and serve with the cabbage and dipping sauce.
Heat the oil, add the onion, and cook until golden brown, about eight minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and cumin until fragrant, then add the beef, breaking up any lumps.
Cook for five minutes until the beef is no longer pink and most moisture has gone.
Add the tomato, turmeric, salt and 60 ml water, cover, and simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Stir in the peas and 120 ml water, then cover and cook for five more minutes.
Cook uncovered for two minutes until the oil separates from the curry.
Serve with rice or bread. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 600 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 2 cm chunks
240 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for three minutes, then lift the pieces out.
Soften the sliced onion in the same pan for eight minutes, then stir in the cinnamon, cumin and turmeric.
Return the chicken with the stock and tomatoes, season, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens and the chicken is tender.
Pour 250 ml boiling water over the couscous, cover for five minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Spoon the tagine over the couscous. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

recipes.title: Quick chicken and chickpea tagine with couscous

steps.text: Chop the herbs, spinach and spring onions very finely and pat them dry.
Beat the eggs with the turmeric, minced garlic and a pinch of salt, then fold in the greens.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a 20 cm non-stick pan and pour in the mixture.
Cook on medium-low for ten minutes until the base is golden and the top nearly set.
Cut into four wedges, flip each, drizzle in the rest of the oil, and cook five minutes.
Stir the grated garlic into the yoghurt and serve it alongside the wedges.
Covered in the fridge, the kuku keeps for 3 days and slices neatly when cold.

recipes.title: Persian herb kuku with garlic yoghurt

ingredients.text: 340 g pork loin, trimmed and finely chopped by hand

steps.text: Cut the aubergine into 1.5 cm cubes and chop the pork as finely as mince.
Stir the stock, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and chopped chilli together in a bowl.
Fry the garlic and ginger in the hot oil for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry for three minutes until cooked through and lightly browned.
Add the aubergine and stir-fry for three minutes until it starts to brown.
Pour in the sauce, bring to a boil, then cover and braise for eight minutes until tender.
Serve over rice. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 2 green or red chillies, one left whole and slit
1 thumb-sized piece of ginger, roughly chopped

steps.text: Toss the prawns with the turmeric and a pinch of salt, then set aside.
Blend the onion, coriander, garlic, ginger, one chilli and 70 ml water into a smooth paste.
Warm the oil on low heat, add the slit chilli, and fry the paste for three minutes.
Add the prawns and stir for a minute, then add 100 ml water, cover, and cook two minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and lime juice and simmer five minutes until the prawns turn pink.
Taste for salt and serve the curry with steamed rice.

ingredients.text: 5 tbsp finely chopped parsley, plus extra to finish

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and mix the beef, onion, most of the parsley and the spices.
Add the salt and two minced garlic cloves, then mix by hand until evenly combined.
Shape the mixture into about 12 small sausages and set them in a baking dish.
Bake the kofta for 15 minutes until browned on top.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, last garlic clove and hot water into a smooth sauce.
Flip the kofta, pour over the sauce and bake 10 minutes until thickened and browned.
Scatter with parsley and serve with flatbread. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 600 g pork loin, in 4 thin cutlets
4 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying

steps.text: Pound the pork between sheets of baking paper to an even thickness of about 8 mm.
Season both sides with the salt and pepper, then set out flour, beaten egg and crumbs in three dishes.
Coat each cutlet in flour, shake off the excess, dip in egg, then press firmly into the crumbs.
Heat about 1.5 cm of oil in a heavy pan until a crumb sizzles at once.
Fry two schnitzels for 3 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through, then drain on kitchen paper.
Fry the remaining two the same way and serve straight away with lemon wedges for squeezing.
Soak the bread in the milk, then mash it into the beef with the egg, seasoning well.
Knead in a quarter of the onion and one chopped garlic clove, then roll walnut-sized balls.
Roast the meatballs on a tray with a drizzle of oil at 180C for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, soften the remaining onion and garlic in the rest of the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the wine and boil until halved, then stir in the tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Slide in the meatballs and peas and simmer 5 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through.
Serve with crusty bread. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 750 g potatoes, cut into large chunks
350 g salmon fillets, skinned and cubed

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C, then boil the potato chunks in salted water until tender.
Drain and mash the potatoes with the butter and milk until smooth and fluffy.
Simmer the cubed fish in a pan of water for 5 minutes, then drain well.
Return the fish to the pan with the peas, cream and parsley and warm gently for 2 minutes.
Spoon the fish into an ovenproof dish, cover with mash and rough up the top with a fork.
Bake for 10 minutes until the top is golden and the edges are bubbling.

recipes.title: Quick salmon and cod fish pie

steps.text: Chop the aubergine and courgette, salt them and leave 10 minutes while you chop the rest.
Fry the aubergine in a tablespoon of oil for 7 minutes, add the courgette and cook 4 more.
Tip the vegetables onto a plate, then add another spoon of oil to the same pan.
Cook the onion, pepper and oregano for 8 minutes until soft, adding the garlic at the end.
Return the aubergine and courgette with the tomatoes, remaining oil and a little salt, then simmer until thickened.
Scatter with basil and serve with rice or crusty bread. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Warm half the oil and garlic, add the tomatoes and half the salt, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C, then pound the chicken between baking paper until about 1 cm thick.
Mix the crumbs with the Parmesan and remaining salt, then coat each breast in flour, egg and crumbs.
Lay the chicken on an oiled rack and bake for 15 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Spoon sauce over each breast, top with mozzarella, and grill on high for 3 minutes until melted and golden.
Rest the chicken for 2 minutes, then serve with the rest of the sauce and a green salad.

ingredients.text: 300 g chicken breast, sliced in half horizontally
200 g canned black beans, drained and roughly mashed

steps.text: Rub the chicken with oil and 1 tsp paprika, sear 3 minutes a side, then rest and chop.
Stir the flour into a tablespoon of oil in a saucepan, then whisk in stock, tomatoes and half the paprika.
Simmer for 5 minutes, whisking often, until the sauce thickens to a thin syrup.
Soften the onion in the chicken pan, then stir in the beans and chicken for 2 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180C, fill the tortillas with the mixture and half the cheese, then roll them up.
Lay them seam down in a dish, pour over the sauce, scatter the remaining cheese and bake for 20 minutes.

ingredients.text: 2 bell peppers, one red and one yellow, diced

steps.text: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper, then brown it in the oil for 5 minutes.
Lift the chicken out, then cook the onion and peppers in the same pan until soft.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and tomato paste, then toast the rice until it smells nutty.
Nestle the chicken into the rice, pour in the stock, bring to a simmer and cover tightly.
Cook on low for 18 minutes until the rice has absorbed the stock and the chicken is cooked through.
Scatter over the peas and rest, covered, for 5 minutes. In the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 4 pork loin chops, about 200 g each
800 g baby potatoes, larger ones halved

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C, toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and the salt, and spread on a tray.
Roast the potatoes for 10 minutes while you stir the ketchup, soy, Worcestershire, sugar, garlic, vinegar and oil together.
Coat both sides of the chops in the rub, keeping a spoonful back for basting.
Push the potatoes aside, add the chops to the tray and roast for 14 minutes.
Switch to the grill, flip the chops, spoon over the spare rub and grill 8 minutes until caramelised.
Rest the chops for 3 minutes, then serve with the potatoes and spoonfuls of the sticky pan juices.

recipes.title: Sticky oven pork chops with potatoes

steps.text: Boil a big pot of salted water for the noodles, and toss the chicken in flour, paprika and salt.
Soften the onion and pepper in the oil for 4 minutes in a wide, deep pot.
Push them aside, add the coated chicken and brown it for 6 minutes, turning, then stir everything together.
Pour in the stock, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is tender.
While that simmers, cook the noodles for the time on the packet, then drain.
Uncover and boil hard for 2 minutes, then take the pot off the heat and stir in the yoghurt.
Taste for salt and spoon the chicken over the noodles. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.

ingredients.text: 2 slices white bread, crusts removed, cubed

steps.text: Grate the onion into a bowl, add the bread cubes and let them soften in the juices.
Add the beef, egg and salt and mix well, then roll into 20 to 24 small balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil in two batches for 3 minutes each, turning, then set aside.
Pour off excess fat, melt the butter in the pan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the stock a little at a time until smooth, then add the meatballs and their juices.
Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the gravy thickens and the meatballs are cooked through.
Stir in the cream, simmer 2 minutes and serve. Covered in the fridge, it keeps for 3 days.
Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20cm square tin with baking parchment.
Melt the butter and honey gently in a small pan, then stir in the oats and sugar until coated.
Press the mixture firmly into the tin, then bake for about 20 minutes until golden.
Let it cool and firm up in the tin, then cut it into nine squares.

ingredients.text: 1 tsp vegetable oil, for the baking sheet

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and lightly oil a baking sheet.
Mash the bananas in a bowl, then stir in the oats, cinnamon, salt and water until evenly mixed.
Shape the mixture into 12 rounds on the tray, about 5 cm wide, pressing each one flat.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes until a knife inserted in the centre comes out dry, then cool.
Slice the green cabbage finely, shred the carrots and grate the onion, then tip everything into a big bowl.
Stir in the mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar until coated, then serve now or chill for 30 minutes.

ingredients.text: 1 tsp vegetable oil, for the ramekins

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and lightly oil four ramekins with the vegetable oil.
Blend the oats to a fine flour, then add the banana, honey, eggs and cinnamon and blend until smooth.
Stir in most of the blueberries, divide the batter between the ramekins and scatter the rest on top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until well risen and springy under a gentle press, then serve warm.
Wrap each pepper in foil and roast over a low hob flame, turning, until the skins char.
Unwrap carefully, let them cool slightly, then peel away the skin and seeds, and chop them.
Pulse the walnuts, garlic, cumin, sugar and salt in a food processor until coarsely ground.
Add the peppers, olive oil and lemon juice, and process until smooth.
Taste, adjust the salt if needed, and serve with warm pitta or vegetable sticks.

recipes.title: Roasted red pepper and walnut dip

steps.text: Set the grill to high and prick the aubergine several times before laying it on a baking tray.
Grill for about 30 minutes, turning halfway, until the skin is charred and the flesh collapses.
Once cool, split the skin, scoop out the flesh and juices, and discard the charred skin.
Mash in the tahini, olive oil, lemon, garlic, salt and pepper, then taste and adjust.
Chill the dip until it firms up, then serve scattered with the parsley.

ingredients.text: 60 ml double cream, in place of cream cheese
1 tbsp vegetable oil, for greasing the tin

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C, 180C fan, and grease a 12-hole muffin tin with the oil.
Whisk the eggs well, then whisk in the cream until the mixture is smooth and even.
Stir through the peas and sweetcorn, season with salt and pepper, and share between the holes.
Bake for around 10 minutes, until set and lightly golden, then leave to cool briefly.
Warm the oil in an ovenproof pan, then soften the courgette and onion gently for 3 to 4 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper, then stir in the mint and 60 g feta.
Pour the eggs over the vegetables and cook on the hob for 3 to 4 minutes until the base sets.
Finish under a hot grill for 4 to 5 minutes until set, then scatter the remaining feta and mint.

ingredients.text: 1/2 green or red bell pepper, diced

steps.text: Prick the potatoes with a fork and microwave them on high for about 4 minutes until partly cooked.
Dice the cooled potatoes, then fry them with the bell pepper, onion, garlic and spices in hot oil.
Press everything into a packed layer, cover, and cook 4 to 5 minutes, then flip and repeat until browned.
Fry the eggs in a little oil until the whites are set, then serve them on the hash.
Heat the oven to 200C, then divide the mushrooms and tomatoes between four ovenproof dishes.
Add the garlic, a little oil and some seasoning to each dish, then bake for 10 minutes.
Tip the spinach into a colander, pour boiling water over until it wilts, then squeeze it dry and add it.
Make a small hollow in each dish, break in an egg and bake 8 to 10 minutes more.
Fry the onion, courgette, mushroom and pepper in hot oil over high heat for 4 minutes.
Stir in the basil, salt and pepper, then make four gaps and crack an egg into each.
Cover the pan with a baking sheet and cook for about 3 minutes until the eggs are set.
Season to taste and serve straight away with toast.
Heat the oil and butter in a large pan, add the mushrooms and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in the oregano and garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the cream and parsley, then simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until thickened, seasoning to taste.
Toast the bread, spoon the mushrooms over the slices and serve straight away.

ingredients.text: 2 garlic cloves, one chopped and one smashed
250 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Coarsely grate the tomatoes and onion into a bowl, then mix in the chilli, chopped garlic, cumin and salt.
Warm 2 teaspoons of the oil in a pan and fry the salsa over low heat for 3 minutes.
In the same pan, mash the beans with the smashed garlic and a spoonful of salsa until hot.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the oil, warm the tortillas, then top each with beans, egg and salsa.

ingredients.text: 280 g canned tuna in water, drained

steps.text: Mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise, celery, onion, lemon juice and salt until combined.
Build each sandwich with lettuce, a generous scoop of tuna, tomato and cheese, then close with bread.
Halve each sandwich if you wish, then serve straight away.
Cook the pasta in plenty of salted boiling water until just tender, then drain and leave to cool.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, garlic, oregano and salt together in a small jar or bowl.
Combine the cooled pasta with the tomatoes, cucumber, feta and parsley in a large bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss well, then serve now or chill for 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Cucumber, tomato and feta pasta salad

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then cook it covered in the cold water until the liquid is fully absorbed.
While the rice cooks, drain the tuna and mix it with the mayonnaise and soy sauce until smooth.
When the rice is cool enough to handle, dampen your hands and rub a little salt onto your palms.
Press a portion of rice into a well in your palm, add a little filling, then cover with rice.
Press the rice into a firm triangle, turning it as you go, then repeat with the rest.

ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds, to garnish

steps.text: Rinse the rice well and cook it as the packet says, then leave it aside.
Dice the salmon small, then toss it with the spring onion, soy sauce, sesame oil and salt.
Refrigerate the salmon mixture while you prepare the avocado and cucumber.
Peel and dice the avocado and cucumber, then divide the rice between two bowls.
Top each bowl with half the salmon, the avocado and cucumber, and scatter sesame seeds over.

ingredients.text: 400 g boneless chicken thigh, diced small

steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a large pot, then soften the carrot, celery and onion for about 7 minutes.
Add the garlic for a minute, then pour in the stock with the oregano and bring to a boil.
Add the diced chicken and noodles, then simmer about 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked and noodles tender.
Stir in the parsley, season to taste and serve straight away.

ingredients.text: 200 g tomatoes, seeded and finely diced

steps.text: Put the couscous in a large bowl, pour over the boiling water, cover, and leave for 20 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork, let it cool, then stir in the vegetables and herbs.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and salt together in a small bowl.
Toss the dressing through the salad until coated, then serve now or chill for 30 minutes.

ingredients.text: 1 can (540 g) black beans, not drained

steps.text: Cook the brown rice following the packet instructions, then divide it between three bowls.
Tip the beans and their liquid into a pan with the cumin and garlic, and warm for about 5 minutes.
Divide the beans, sweetcorn and tomatoes among the bowls, then top with cheese, spring onion and chilli.
Cool any bowls you are saving and cover them; each bowl keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Fry the onion gently in the oil until soft, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the stock, then add the sweetcorn and potato and boil for about 20 minutes until tender.
Mash the potato lightly, then stir in the salt and milk and warm through.
Mix the flour with a little water to a smooth paste, stir it in and simmer for 5 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot, with soft bread rolls alongside.

ingredients.text: 240 g canned chickpeas (one 400 g can), drained and patted dry

steps.text: Pulse the garlic, chickpeas, cumin, salt and breadcrumbs in a food processor until it holds together but keeps some texture.
Shape the mixture into small patties, pressing them firmly so they hold together.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the patties for about 5 minutes per side until golden.
Warm the pitta, then fill with lettuce, tomato and falafel and finish with a drizzle of the thinned tahini.
Zest the lemon, then warm the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the garlic and salt and cook for about one minute until fragrant.
Tip in the tomatoes, lemon zest, spaghetti and boiling water, then press the pasta under the liquid with tongs.
Cover and cook for four minutes, stirring now and then so the pasta stays submerged.
Uncover and simmer for six to eight minutes until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the Parmesan.
Cover and rest for five minutes, then taste, season and scatter over the torn basil leaves.

ingredients.text: 710 ml water, plus more as needed

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat, then stir in the pepper for about a minute.
Add the pasta, salt and water, using just enough water to barely cover the pasta.
Raise the heat to high and stir often, adding small splashes of water only if needed.
Cook until the pasta is nearly al dente, then take the pan off the heat.
Sprinkle in the cheese gradually, stirring all the while, until it melts into a glossy sauce that coats the pasta.
If the sauce seizes up, return the pan to low heat and loosen it with a splash of water.
Serve at once with a little more cracked pepper and grated cheese on top.

ingredients.text: 330 g canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed
85 g small pasta, such as bows or rotini

steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat, then add the onion, garlic, carrot and celery.
Cook for seven to eight minutes, stirring often, until the vegetables begin to soften.
Add the tomatoes, stock, oregano and beans, then bring the pot to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the pasta and simmer for ten to fifteen minutes until tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste, then serve hot.

ingredients.text: 240 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 medium sweet potato, cut into small cubes

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 C and dry the chickpeas in a tea towel, rubbing off loose skins.
Toss the chickpeas and sweet potato on a lined tray with half the oil, spices, garlic and salt.
Roast for twenty minutes, then toss the mixture and push it to one side of the tray.
Add the broccoli and red onion to the cleared space with the remaining oil, then spread out.
Roast for a further twelve minutes until the sweet potato is tender and the broccoli is charred.
Scatter the chopped parsley over the tray and serve while everything is still warm.

recipes.title: Smoky sweet potato and chickpea sheet-pan dinner

ingredients.text: 1 lemon, zested and juiced, plus slices to serve

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 C and grease a large rimmed baking tray.
Mix the melted butter with the lemon zest and juice, garlic, parsley, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Toss the courgette, potato and green beans with the olive oil and spread them on the tray.
Roast the vegetables for 15 minutes until the potatoes start to soften.
Remove the tray, add the cherry tomatoes and push the vegetables aside to make room for the cod.
Place the cod in the gaps, brush with the lemon butter, and top with lemon slices.
Spoon the rest of the lemon butter over the vegetables and bake for 15 to 20 minutes.
Check the cod flakes easily, then serve straight from the tray with any pan juices.

ingredients.text: 65 g plain flour, seasoned with salt and pepper

steps.text: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Dredge the chicken in seasoned flour and brown for about five minutes a side, in batches if crowded.
Remove the chicken, then add the mushrooms to the same pan and saute for about eight minutes.
Add the garlic for a minute, then pour in the wine, scraping up the browned bits from the base.
Return the chicken to the pan and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, then lift the chicken out again.
Stir in the cream, Parmesan and mustard, season to taste, then return the chicken for two minutes.
Season both sides of the pork chops with the salt, pepper and cinnamon, then let them rest.
Heat one tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the chops in the hot oil for three to four minutes until well browned underneath.
Flip the chops and cook four to five minutes, until the centre reaches 63 C, then move to a plate.
Slice the apples thinly and cut the onion into wedges while you whisk the broth with the mustard.
Melt the butter with the remaining oil in the pan, then add the apples and onion.
Saute for two to three minutes, pour in the broth mixture and scrape up the browned bits.
Simmer for two to three minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce looks glossy.
Return the chops to the pan among the apples, spoon the sauce over them, then serve.

recipes.title: Pork chops with apples and onions

steps.text: Brown the beef and onion in a large deep pan over medium heat, breaking up the meat.
Drain off the fat, then stir in the garlic, tomato paste and cumin for about one minute.
Pour in the tomatoes, stock and milk, then bring to a low boil.
Stir in the pasta, cover and simmer, stirring now and then, until the pasta is tender.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the cheddar until melted and creamy, then serve straight away.

ingredients.text: 439 g canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Brown the mince in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat, crumbling it with a spoon as it cooks.
Stir in the onion, carrot and garlic and keep cooking over medium heat until the pieces turn soft.
Pour in the stock, tomatoes, beans, cumin, paprika and salt, then let it simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Ladle the chilli into bowls and add whichever toppings you like.

recipes.title: Classic beef and kidney bean chilli

ingredients.text: 4 cod fillets, skin on, about 150 g each
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus black pepper to taste

steps.text: Dry the cod well with paper towels, then sprinkle salt and pepper over both sides.
Warm the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat until it is almost smoking.
Lay the fillets in skin side down and leave them for four to five minutes, until golden and crisp.
Turn the fillets and cook two to three minutes more, until opaque and flaky, then lift them onto a plate.
In the same pan, melt the butter, add the garlic and cook for about thirty seconds until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the lemon juice and let it bubble briefly, then take the pan off the heat.
