Stir in the zest and parsley, spoon the sauce over the cod and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Pan-seared cod with garlic lemon butter

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet and soften the onion, pepper and garlic for four minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste for 30 seconds, then add the minced beef and break it up.
Cook the beef for about six minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in the tomatoes, cumin, salt and black pepper, then cover and turn the heat low.
Simmer covered for 10 to 12 minutes until the flavours have come together.
Taste the sauce, adjust the salt and serve it warm.

ingredients.text: 100 g pork loin, cut into small lardons
2 small bell peppers, seeded and cut into strips

steps.text: Use a deep saucepan rather than a frying pan, so the juices do not evaporate too fast.
Fry the pork lardons in the oil over medium heat for five minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the diced onion and cook for five minutes, stirring regularly.
Stir in the sliced garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then add the peppers, tomatoes and paprika.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 25 minutes until thick and rich.
Taste after about five minutes and add salt only if it needs it.

ingredients.text: 250 g pork loin, cut into chunks

steps.text: Cut the pork loin into chunks and fry it in the oil over medium heat until browned.
Add the onion and garlic and fry for two to three minutes until softened.
Add the shredded cabbage and fry until it starts to soften and wilt.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer on low heat for about 20 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, oregano and salt, then cook for a minute.
Take the pan off the heat and serve with bread; the skillet keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 225 g green beans, trimmed and halved
115 g canned tuna in water, drained and flaked

steps.text: Boil the eggs for about 8 minutes, then cool them in iced water, peel and halve them.
Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes, then add the green beans for 4 minutes, cooling each in iced water.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, salt and garlic together in a small jar or bowl.
Spread the lettuce on a platter, then arrange the eggs, potatoes, beans, tomatoes and tuna on top.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad just before serving, and season with a little extra salt.

ingredients.text: 2 spring onions, green parts only, finely sliced

steps.text: Cook the pork in the hot oil for a few minutes, breaking it up as it browns.
Add the garlic, then the wine and soy sauce, and cook until the pork is fragrant and cooked through.
Mix the tahini, chilli flakes, vinegar and spring onion greens in a bowl to make the sauce.
Boil the noodles until tender, then drain them and set aside 100 ml of the cooking water.
Divide the sauce between two bowls, add the pork, noodles and reserved water, then mix well at the table.

ingredients.text: 100 g cabbage, cut into large chunks
1/2 small carrot, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Toss the pork with the wine and a little soy sauce, then rest it for five minutes.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until just tender, then drain them well.
Heat half the oil in a wok and stir-fry the pork until no longer pink, then set aside.
Add the rest of the oil, then stir-fry the onion, cabbage and carrot with salt until the cabbage softens.
Push the vegetables aside, add the noodles and sprinkle over the wine, then stir-fry until hot.
Return the pork, pour in the Worcestershire sauce and soy sauce, and toss until well coated.
Serve straight away, piled high on plates while the noodles are still hot.

ingredients.text: 125 g broccoli, cut into short pieces

steps.text: Soak the dried noodles in hot water until flexible, about ten minutes, then drain them well.
Slice the chicken thinly across the grain and cut the broccoli into short pieces.
Stir together the garlic, fish sauce, soy sauce, chilli flakes and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat a wok until very hot, add three tablespoons of oil and fry the noodles until lightly caramelised.
Set the noodles aside, add the remaining oil and fry the chicken until nearly cooked.
Add the broccoli and fry for two minutes, then return the noodles and pour over the sauce.
Toss gently to coat, push the noodles aside, scramble the beaten egg, then mix everything together.
Give everything a final toss and serve at once on a plate.

ingredients.text: 1 red pepper, cut into thin batons

steps.text: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for five minutes until just tender, then rinse and drain.
Beat the eggs, scramble them in a little oil until just set, then lift them out.
Stir-fry the garlic, pepper and curry powder over high heat for about two minutes.
Add the shredded chicken and prawns, then the noodles and soy sauce, tossing with tongs.
Return the scrambled egg and spring onion, toss again until evenly coloured, then serve at once.
Smear a little oil over the aubergine, pierce the skin, and blacken it over an open flame until soft.
Once cool enough to handle, strip away the burnt skin and roughly chop or mash the flesh.
Heat the rest of the oil and fry the cumin until it sizzles, then add the onion.
Cook the onion for about three minutes until it turns light pink.
Add the ginger, garlic and chilli and cook for a minute, then stir in the tomato.
Cook the tomato for two minutes, then add the curry powder until the oil separates.
Stir in the mashed aubergine and salt, cook on low for three to four minutes, then serve.

ingredients.text: 400 g chicken breast, cut into chunks

steps.text: Soften the diced onion in a little oil in a wide pan over fairly high heat, about five minutes.
Tip in the chicken and turn it for about three minutes, until white all over.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and curry powder, then cook for two minutes, stirring often.
Pour in the yoghurt and cream, then stir in the ground almonds and sugar and bring up to the boil.
Let it bubble gently for five to six minutes, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through.
Taste for seasoning and spoon over basmati rice to serve.

ingredients.text: 1 red bell pepper, cut into pieces

steps.text: Mix the garlic, ginger, paprika, curry powder and coconut milk with the chicken and marinate for ten minutes.
Soften the onion and pepper in the oil in a wide pan, covered, over gentle heat for five minutes.
Raise the heat and brown the chicken for three to five minutes.
Pour in the blended tomatoes with half of the leftover coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for ten minutes, loosening with more coconut milk if the sauce gets too thick.
Serve with rice or naan once the curry has thickened and the chicken is cooked through.

ingredients.text: 225 g pork loin, sliced into thin strips

steps.text: Boil the noodles until just tender, then drain and rinse them in cold water.
Toss the pork strips with a spoonful of soy sauce, then leave them to marinate for fifteen minutes.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and minced garlic in a bowl.
Blanch the spinach briefly until wilted, then refresh it in cold water and squeeze dry.
Stir-fry the onion and carrot in a little sesame oil until just tender, then tip into a large bowl.
Cook the beaten eggs into a thin omelette, roll it up and slice it into strips.
Stir-fry the pork in the hot pan until cooked through, then add it to the bowl with the vegetables.
Add the noodles and sauce to the pan and toss over medium heat for three to four minutes.
Return the bowl's vegetables, pork and egg to the pan, toss well and serve warm.
Cook the chicken in the hot oil with half the curry powder for about five minutes, then set it aside.
Fry the onions in the same pan for about seven minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the ginger, garlic and peppers for two minutes, then add the tomatoes and mash them as they cook.
Add the rest of the curry powder for a minute, then return the chicken and the green chillies.
Pour in the water, cover and let it simmer gently for ten to fifteen minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Switch off once the sauce is thick, then serve with rice or chapatis.

ingredients.text: 1 small bunch fresh coriander, to garnish

steps.text: Cut the chicken into bite-sized cubes and chop the onion and tomatoes finely.
Cube half the ginger and cut the rest into thin matchsticks for later.
Warm the oil in a large pan and fry the onion until deep golden, about six minutes.
Add the cubed ginger and cook briefly, just until fragrant, without letting it darken.
Stir in the tomatoes, turmeric, salt and chilli, then simmer until the sauce thickens and reduces.
Add the chicken with about a quarter cup of water and stir-fry until oil separates onto the sauce.
Stir in the remaining ginger, take the pan off the heat and scatter fresh coriander over.

ingredients.text: 300 g chicken breast, cut into small pieces

steps.text: Fry half the garlic in oil until lightly browned, then set the garlic oil aside.
Heat more oil and pour it over the chilli flakes to make a chilli oil, then set aside.
Fry the onion and remaining garlic in oil until lightly browned, then add the chicken and stir for two minutes.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce and water, then cover and simmer for five minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Boil the rice noodles until just chewy, drain them and divide between bowls.
Spoon the chicken curry over each portion, drizzle with chilli oil and garlic oil, top with spring onion.
Mix the beef, onion, garlic, tomato, salt and spices in a bowl until just combined.
If you have time, cover and chill the filling for an hour so the flavours settle.
Heat the oven to 200 C, or 400 F, and line a baking sheet.
Cut a slit along the side of each pita and open it into a pocket.
Spoon in about a third of a cup of filling and press it into an even layer inside.
Brush both sides of each stuffed pita with melted butter and lay them on the sheet.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the meat is cooked through and the bread is golden.
Cut each hawawshi into halves and serve with tahini, salad or pickles.

ingredients.text: 1 kg boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into pieces
600 ml chicken stock, in place of water

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for about 10 minutes until nearly tender, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion, garlic and cumin for three minutes.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for three minutes, then splash in a little stock to deglaze.
Add the chicken pieces, stir to coat them in the spiced base and season with salt.
Pour in the remaining stock, then add the potatoes and spinach and bring to the boil.
Reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Taste and adjust the salt, simmer uncovered for a thicker gravy if you like.
Serve the curry hot with rice or bread while the gravy is still thick.

recipes.title: Trinidadian curry chicken with potato and spinach

ingredients.text: 600 g skinless cod fillets, cut into four portions
1 medium carrot, cut into thin matchsticks
1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
1 small courgette, cut into thin matchsticks
1 small red chilli, seeded and sliced

steps.text: Season the fish with a teaspoon of the salt and chill it for a few hours or overnight.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick skillet over high heat.
Fry the fish for about five minutes each side until crisp, then drain it on a rack.
Put the vegetables, chilli, vinegar, sugar and remaining salt into a saucepan with a spoon of frying oil.
Bring to a boil and simmer for about three minutes until most of the liquid is absorbed.
Spoon the hot pickle over the fried fish in a covered dish.
Cover and marinate overnight, then serve the fish the next day.

ingredients.text: 900 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into pieces

steps.text: Fry the sliced onion in the oil over medium heat until golden brown.
Add the chicken, garlic, cumin, cinnamon and black pepper, then brown the chicken for about five minutes.
Stir in the rice and cook for two minutes, coating each grain in the oil and spices.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, then bring the pot to a simmer.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Turn off the heat, rest the pot covered for five minutes, then fluff the rice and serve.

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp chopped mint, plus 1/4 cup torn mint leaves for the salad

steps.text: Squeeze as much moisture as you can from the grated courgette, using a tea towel.
Mix the courgette with the feta, chopped mint, breadcrumbs, eggs and half the sliced onion.
Lightly oil a non-stick frying pan and cook heaped tablespoons of the mix over medium-high heat.
Cook each batch for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden, making 16 fritters in total.
Toss the tomato, remaining mint and remaining onion together to make a simple salad.
Serve the fritters warm with the salad and a spoonful of yoghurt on the side.

ingredients.text: 3 large boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut in half lengthwise

steps.text: Cut each chicken breast in half lengthwise, then season the cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet lightly in flour, shake off the excess, and set them on a plate.
Heat the oil and 2 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the cutlets in batches for 2 to 4 minutes per side, until cooked through and golden.
Move the cooked cutlets to a warm plate, then fry the rest with 1 tablespoon each of oil and butter.
Pour the wine and lemon juice into the pan, scraping up the browned bits, then simmer for one minute.
Return the chicken to the sauce and spoon it over the cutlets as they warm.
Whisk in the remaining butter and chopped parsley, then serve the chicken with the sauce.

ingredients.text: 40 ml ketchup, plus extra to serve
60 ml water (30 ml for the sauce, 30 ml for the eggs)
2 tbsp vegetable oil (1 for the filling, 1 for the omelettes)
2 cups cold cooked white rice, leftover

steps.text: Whisk the ketchup, water and soy sauce together in a small bowl and set aside.
Fry the mushrooms in 1 tablespoon of the oil over medium heat for about 5 minutes until browned.
Add the onion, carrot and peas and cook for 3 minutes until the carrot is just tender.
Tip in the rice, break it up, then pour in the ketchup mixture and stir until evenly coloured.
For each omelette, whisk two eggs with a tablespoon of water.
Heat a little of the remaining oil in a medium pan, pour in the eggs and swirl until mostly set.
Spoon half the rice onto the omelette, fold the sides in, and turn it out onto a plate.
Top with ketchup and repeat the omelette steps for the second serving.

ingredients.text: 450 g chicken breast, cut into 4 cutlets
1/2 tsp salt, plus extra to finish
500 ml vegetable oil, for shallow frying
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, for the sauce

steps.text: Pound the chicken to an even thickness of about 1/4 inch, then season both sides with salt and pepper.
Set out three shallow dishes with flour, beaten egg and panko.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip it in egg, then press it firmly into the panko to coat.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium heat to 170 C.
Fry the cutlets two at a time for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with a pinch of salt, then slice into strips.
Stir the ketchup and Worcestershire together and serve the strips with the sauce.

ingredients.text: 400 g large raw prawns, peeled and deveined
100 g plain flour, plus 2 tbsp for dusting
1 litre vegetable oil, for deep frying
1 tbsp soy sauce, for the dipping sauce
1 tbsp white wine vinegar, for the dipping sauce
1 1/2 tsp sugar, for the dipping sauce
1/4 tsp grated ginger, for the dipping sauce

steps.text: Peel and devein the prawns, make shallow cuts on the underside and top, then press them flat.
Season the prawns with salt, then dust them lightly with flour and set aside.
Whisk the egg into the cold water, then add the flour and stir gently, leaving small lumps.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170 C and test it with a drop of batter.
Dip each prawn in the batter, let the excess drip off, then lower it into the oil.
Fry in small batches for two to three minutes, turning occasionally, until crisp.
Drain on a wire rack, then whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and ginger into a dipping sauce.

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp plain flour, 2 for the patties and 2 for the gravy
2 cups chicken stock, for the gravy
1 tbsp soy sauce, for the gravy

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the milk, 2 tablespoons flour and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in the chopped mushrooms and cooked shredded chicken, mixing evenly.
Heat half the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Spoon in the egg mixture to make three or four small patties and cook 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Repeat with the remaining oil and mixture, draining the patties on kitchen paper.
Whisk the remaining flour into the stock with the soy sauce and sugar in a small pan.
Simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the gravy thickens.
Place the patties on a plate, spoon the gravy over them and serve.

ingredients.text: 450 g floury potatoes, cut into chunks
1 lemon, zest of half and the rest cut into wedges

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in a covered pan of water for 12 to 15 minutes until tender.
Preheat the grill, then season the salmon and grill it for 5 to 6 minutes until just cooked.
Drain the potatoes and steam dry, then mash. Break the cooled salmon into large flakes.
Mix the mash with the ketchup, mustard, lemon zest, parsley and a pinch of seasoning.
Gently fold in the flaked salmon, then shape into four large fish cakes.
Coat each cake in flour, dip it in the beaten egg, then press it into the breadcrumbs.
Fry the cakes in hot oil over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve warm with lemon wedges and a green salad.

ingredients.text: 4 eggs, boiled and peeled, plus 1 beaten egg
225 g minced pork loin, in place of sausage meat
50 g plain flour, for dusting and coating
1 litre vegetable oil, for deep frying

steps.text: Simmer the eggs for 9 minutes, then cool them under cold water and peel.
Mix the pork with the parsley, spring onion, salt and pepper, and divide into four portions.
Flatten each portion on a floured surface to roughly 13 by 8 centimetres.
Dust each egg in flour, set it in the middle of a portion and wrap the meat around it.
Smooth the coating, dip each one in the beaten egg, then roll in the breadcrumbs until coated.
Heat the oil until a cube of bread sizzles, then fry the scotch eggs for 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain on kitchen paper and cool; serve warm or cold.
Preheat the grill and set an oven rack 10 to 12 centimetres below the heat.
Wilt the spinach in the microwave for about 3 minutes, then drain well and chop coarsely.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a 12-inch ovenproof skillet and cook the onion until lightly browned.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl and stir in the spinach, feta, oregano, salt and pepper.
Add the remaining 2 teaspoons of oil to the skillet, tilt to coat, then pour in the egg mixture.
Leave it over medium heat undisturbed for about 7 minutes, until only the surface is still runny.
Grill for about 2 minutes until the top browns, then slide onto a board and cut into wedges.

ingredients.text: 180 ml vegetable stock, in place of dashi
225 g pork loin, thinly sliced into 8 pieces

steps.text: Whisk the flour with the vegetable stock until smooth and set the batter aside.
Shred the cabbage finely, then wash and dry it thoroughly in a salad spinner.
Beat the eggs into the batter, then fold in the cabbage in three portions.
Heat a little oil in two lidded frying pans over medium heat, to cook two pancakes at once.
Spoon in the batter, shape each into a thick round about 15 cm across and lay pork slices on top.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, until the base is browned.
Flip the pancakes, press gently to reshape and cover again for 5 minutes.
Flip one last time and cook uncovered for 2 minutes until the pancakes are cooked through.
Mix the ketchup and Worcestershire sauce together in a small bowl for the sauce.
Spread the sauce over each pancake, drizzle with mayonnaise and scatter over the spring onion.
